Lennar Master Program: 8.5% on $5,874M invested (63.5% of the book)
Other builders: 10.8% on $3,371M (36.5%), including the 12% Dream Finders preferred. Blended 9.3% on $9,245M
How to read it (ours): The 230bp gap between Lennar and everyone else is the price of the founder relationship.

Lennar Master Program: Flat at 8.5% every quarter since the spin
How to read it (ours): The premium over Lennar narrowed from about 320bp to about 230bp in 18 months as the book grew. Management blames lower SOFR and a tilt to stronger builders, not spread cuts. Compiled by us from the quarterly releases.

Lennar Master Program: Lennar Master Program: $484.8M of 2025 option fees (85%)
Other builders: Lennar-related ventures paid about $16.7M more, and about $303M of 12% paid-in-kind development loans in the bucket were Lennar related-party balances (Sep 2025). Builders independent of Lennar paid $69.4M, 12% of 2025 option fees
How to read it (ours): The headline "36% outside Lennar" overstates the independent book; through 2025 roughly nine-tenths of fee income was Lennar or Lennar-related.

Lennar Master Program: Seed assets: fixed 8.5%. New Lennar deals: 3-year BBB bond index + 4.00% +/- a rating adjustment, floor 7%, cap 10%, then fixed for the project's life
Other builders: Mostly floating with a floor. Deck (Feb 2025): SOFR + 600 to 900bp. Calls (2026): floors average about 10% and sit 50 to 200bp under the current rate
How to read it (ours): Floors near 10% mean non-Lennar yields cannot fall far even if SOFR does.

Term: Target pricing by builder type (Millrose deck, Feb 2025)
Lennar Master Program: 8.5% fixed, 5% initial deposit
Other builders: "Strategic" builders: 9 to 12% with about a 10% deposit. "Third-party" builders: 10 to 13% with a 10 to 20% deposit. Deals of $10M to $100M, 6 to 60 months
How to read it (ours): Management estimates at launch. First $250M outside Lennar closed above 11% (March 2025).

Lennar Master Program: 5% of projected land and development cost up front, plus up to 5% more that Millrose can call or that falls due on walk-away
Other builders: About 10% today, versus roughly 20 to 25% historically for land banking (CEO, Q2 2026 call)
How to read it (ours): Millrose trades deposit for pooling. Book-wide, builder deposits were $1,003M against $9,902M of homesites under option, about 10%.

Lennar Master Program: Land cost plus the pre-set development budget. No premium or escalator: the option fee is the whole return
Other builders: Not disclosed

Lennar Master Program: Forfeit the 5%, owe the rest of the additional 5%, finish horizontal work in the pool, and Millrose may cancel the options on every other property in that pool. Lennar's money at risk is capped at $50M per seed pool and $25M per new pool; 30 pools averaging 29 properties
Other builders: 95 to 96% of all invested capital is in cross-termination pools (2026 calls). The prospectus warns pooling "is not guaranteed" for other customers
How to read it (ours): The cap means abandoning a whole Lennar seed pool of roughly $500M of takedown value costs at most $50M (our arithmetic: cap / 10%).

Lennar Master Program: Not a default: the option simply ends. Millrose keeps the option money and can claim direct damages but cannot force a purchase
Other builders: Not disclosed

Lennar Master Program: Up to four quarterly takedown extensions with no stated fee; up to two six-month pauses per property at half rate (trigger: 10% local home-price fall, or Lennar's discretion under the Founder's Rights Agreement); can accelerate up to 50% of a pool
Other builders: Not disclosed
How to read it (ours): A pause halves Millrose's income on that property for up to a year (two with consent).

Lennar Master Program: If Millrose gives any other builder a lower rate, Lennar can take that rate on its new deals for the next 180 days
Other builders: n/a
How to read it (ours): Every cheap deal Millrose writes for a third party can reprice Lennar's forward flow. This puts a soft floor under its third-party pricing.

Lennar Master Program: Millrose funds horizontal work up to a fixed contract sum; Lennar builds it, bears every dollar of overrun, and backs it with an unlimited parent guaranty
Other builders: Individually negotiated through separate subsidiaries; "may resemble traditional land banking". No Lennar-style parent guaranty disclosed

Lennar Master Program: 3.8 years
Other builders: 2.4 years (total book 3.3 years)

Lennar Master Program: From 2026-03-01 Lennar can reserve capital each quarter: its recycled capital plus 25% of new non-revolver debt and equity raised beyond the first $2B. While capital is reserved Millrose must buy any Lennar deal that meets the criteria
Other builders: What Lennar does not reserve is available to others
How to read it (ours): Third-party builders are second in line for Millrose capital by contract.

Lennar Master Program: No more than 40% of committed capital in one state. No debt beyond 1:1 debt-to-equity without Lennar's consent
Other builders: No per-builder limit disclosed. Lennar is 63.5% of invested capital (about 58% pro forma for Dream Finders)

Lennar Master Program: Rausch Coleman for Lennar (Feb 2025): $900M of land, 25,000 homesites
Other builders: Landsea for New Home Co (May 2025): $700M, 4,186 homesites. Beazer for Dream Finders (Oct 2026): $580M of land on about 7,000 homesites plus a $488M preferred
How to read it (ours): Three of the largest builder deals of 2025 to 2026 used Millrose as the land buyer.

Lennar Master Program: n/a
Other builders: Land bank: $580M net of deposits, about 2.5-year life, $8.0M commitment fee. Preferred: 12% cumulative, perpetual, callable by Dream Finders from year 3, convertible by Millrose from year 6, $5.25M commitment fee
How to read it (ours): First time Millrose paired a land bank with corporate capital. Commitment fees are about 1.4% of the land and about 1.05% of the $500M preferred (our arithmetic).

Lennar Master Program: No terminations, forfeitures, delinquencies or defaults reported
Other builders: Same. Management says no customer has asked to renegotiate (Q3 2026 call)

Lennar Master Program: Spread of about 230bp on Lennar capital (8.5% yield less about 6.2% blended debt cost); only 175 to 200bp against the new 6.50 to 6.75% bonds
Other builders: About 460bp (10.8% less about 6.2%). The 12% Dream Finders preferred, funded with 6.50 to 6.75% bonds, carries about 525 to 550bp gross
How to read it (ours): Our estimate: Millrose does not state a weighted cost of debt. Inputs are its four bond coupons and SOFR + 1.75 to 2.25% bank debt, shown in the profile.

Lennar Master Program: n/a
Other builders: Debt-to-capitalization 36% at 2026-09-30, above the 33% maximum it stated through Q1 2026 (no target stated since). Bank covenant: net debt / capital up to 0.45x (0.50x after a large acquisition), interest cover 1.5x, tangible net worth $4.39B. No single-builder concentration cap found in the bank or bond documents
How to read it (ours): With no equity below book and 100% AFFO payout, new non-Lennar growth has to come from takedown recycling or covenant headroom.

Lennar Master Program: Kennedy Lewis is paid 1.25% a year of tangible assets ($30.3M in Q3 2026), no incentive fee; removal costs 1.5x to 3.0x the annual fee
Other builders: Same fee on all assets
How to read it (ours): After the fee, Millrose keeps about 7.25% on Lennar capital and about 9.5% on other capital before financing costs (our arithmetic: yield minus 1.25%).
